utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Aditya Menon, Anna Svensson, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends from the OTP, to everyone in and around the courtroom. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, with Nicholas Robson, representing General Rasim Delic, with legal assistants Lejla Gluhic, Lana Deljkic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Madam Vidovic, before we call you, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. I remind you that you are still bound by that declaration. Thank you very much, and I'm sorry for what I just said. Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "PW-8"] [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I hope you rested well and we can continue. Yesterday, we talked about Sheik Enver Saban, and in relation to that, I just want to put one question to you. The Sheik was connected to the activities of the Egyptian Al-Jama'ah, Al-Islamiyah, if I pronounced it correctly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, there were some links, I am aware of that, between Sheik Enver and the Egyptian Samat Al-Islamiyah, although I am not sure if that is true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt, I see that the record states that the name of the witness is PW-8. I thought it was PW-9. We'll just make sure that we know it's PW-9. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now I'm going to ask you something else. It has to do with a group of questions put to you in your statement. It has to do with discipline in the El Mujahedin Detachment. When you talked about the El Mujahedin Detachment, you said, in paragraph 106 of your statement, that the detachment command wanted to have respect, order and discipline, which meant that they should be respected by ordinary, regular people and in the environs; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The detachment had camps that were monitored; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were guards, and it was known who was entering and who was exiting the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the detachment, there were rules of conduct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We saw that the Shura pronounced disciplinary measures and acted as a kind of military tribunal; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, the Shura did hand down disciplinary measures, that is correct, although such measures were also passed down by some responsible people in the detachment, not just by the Shura. There was no military tribunal, as such, within the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that some responsible people and the Shura passed down disciplinary measures. This was not done outside the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, it was done inside the -- or within the detachment structures only.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was done in accordance to the detachment rules?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, according to detachment rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that the Shura and these responsible people in the detachment did not allow interference in affairs that they considered to be their own in the detachment, they did not allow anyone else outside of the detachment to interfere in what they considered to be their own affairs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that members of the detachment were trained also in respect of prisoners of war. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to go into private session, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 666.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, Witness, this is an act of the Security Service Department of the 3rd Corps from the 21st of June, 1995, and again it relates to the events in the El Mujahedin unit. I would now like the witness to look at page 2 of this document. This is page 3 in the English version. Can we scroll down the English version, please. Thank you very much. Can we look at the last paragraph? Witness, I'm going to ask you something. You see a part here that's underlined. Could you please read that? It says here that the information is that "Nebil Al Misi" [phoen] and someone else had set out to the front lines, and since they did not know the way, they found themselves 15 metres from Chetnik lines and the shooting that ensued, the -- Nebil was hit, but Mustafa did not know whether he was killed after that. An operation was carried out. Two Chetniks were killed and two heads were brought." Please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that from this document, we can see that this event, relating to the beheading, took place in action, in the course of an action?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That is one of the cases that I mentioned, and I mentioned all these particulars in my statement. This happened to happen in my zone of responsibility. This was on the 29th of May, 1995. That was when the action was. I don't know the date that is on the document, but I think that that was the time that it happened. It was shortly after the first action on the Zavidovici front.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these people were killed in battle, and then the beheading took place; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put the document away now. I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 665 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the middle of this document, where it says: "During the killing of a member of this unit ..." If you can see that. Perhaps we can scroll down the English version. This relevant part for us begins with the words: "When one of the members ..." Do you see that part? Perhaps it would be the easiest thing if I quoted it. It says: "When one of the members of the El Mujahedin unit was killed, they organised a squad of ten fighters who went out in front of the lines of defence, liquidated a number of Chetniks, slit the throats of two of them, and carried their heads through the villages along the Krivaja River valley." My question to you is: Do you agree that in this document, this same event is being described? Can you please take a look?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, the same event is being described.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was thinking of the event that we discussed in connection with the previous document, number 666. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to draw your attention to paragraph 197 of your statement. You described another event where it is said that the Arabs from the line brought the head of Momir, a policeman. Please, can you tell us what you know about this event that has to do with this beheading?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: This event or incident took place shortly after our second operation on the Vozuca front. Abu Sabit Masri, who was responsible for a section of the line, led a group to -- into reconnaissance towards the Serbian Army lines, and during this reconnaissance a sabotage attack was carried out on several dugouts on the Serb lines. And on that occasion, some -- I think three members of the military police were killed. I think it was either the military or the civilian police, I'm not sure anymore, who happened to be on the line of the Army of Republika Srpska. Their heads were cut off and brought to the village of Livade, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the beheading of Momir, the policeman, in no way can be linked with the beheading of any prisoner of war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, it cannot. I remembered his name. Their documents, IDs, were brought, and a diary was found on one of the policeman, too. I think that they were from Srbac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, if I understood correctly, that you remembered this name. Can you remember this name?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Momir. I'm talking about Momir. That's the name I remembered, I think Momir Mitrovic, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I hear well that the name is Momir Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Witness, did you say "Momir Mitrovic"?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session once again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the Security Service in the detachment that you described was not an organ of the Security Service of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, hierarchially linked with the higher or superior organs of the Military Security Service of the Division or of the Corps, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That is a service formed by the Detachment Command, and it was solely responsible to the Detachment Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What Beganovic actually did was to be in charge of the camp security?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes. That was to take care of the Vatrostalna base that was the Command of the detachment, and also to take care about the discipline of the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment who at that time were in Vatrostalna.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he did not gather data for the Corps security organ?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, not at all, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He did not work according to their instructions, the instructions of the security organ of the 3rd Corps, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, he worked according to Muatez's instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Awad Ajman either did not carry out the duties of a commander, he was a translator, was he not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, Ajman Awad was working as a translator, mostly with Muatez, and he did not have any particular function in the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. I'm just going to ask you to pause between question and answer so that the transcript can keep up with my questions and your answers. Now I would like to put some more questions to you that have to do with the existence of some other services within the detachment. In paragraph 148 of your statement, you mentioned the personnel service, and you said that in the course of 1995, it was better organised. Now I would like to put some questions to you so that we can see what kind of service it was. I want to ask you: The detachment did not have an actual personnel service that registered all the fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The personnel service did keep a register of the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, so I don't know what you're thinking of specifically. That was its assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I mean is this: It did not have a service that took passports from the foreigners, registered them, provided the appropriate municipal organs with the information or the municipal ministry, provided them with information about members of the detachment, something that other army units did? This is what I was thinking of. But can you please wait for the question to be recorded.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The personnel service in the detachment did not do that. There was a separate service for newly-arrived Arabs. That was called "The Command for Arabs," which did something similar to what you are saying now. They would take their passports, et cetera, but the information was not passed on to the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although the 3rd Corps Command insisted on this, did it not? You know that the 3rd Corps Command insisted on this?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. However, they received only information by nicknames, not by the real names of the detachment members.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fighters did not have personal ID cards or register cards?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, they did not have those in the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, at this point I would like to go back briefly into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 591.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the document turns up on our screens, in the detachment one knew that the Security Service was harbouring a certain amount of mistrust towards the Command and the detachment and that they were holding them under some sort of treatment; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this document now. It's a short document produced by the Security Service Department, dated the 22nd of April, 1995. The heading is: "List of members of the El Mujahedin unit, hereby requested by." Have a look, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Can we zoom in, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in, please. And I can also -- or we can see better now. The witness is done reading. Can we bring the English back on our screens, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, there is an order by the 3rd Corps commander -- or, rather, the document reads that: By an order of the 3rd Corps commander, the manpower levels of the El Mujahedin unit were restricted, and further recruitment of fighters from abroad and domestically was suspended, at least by the 22nd of April, 1995. My question about that -- here we are, April 1995. Did anyone in the detachment actually know that any further recruitment of any sort of members, domestic or foreign, to the El Mujahedin Detachment was, in fact, suspended?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that was a well-known fact. I, myself, saw the order at the time it was issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So was this order complied with?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: New members were being recruited to the very last day of the detachment existence, so the order was not complied with.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now for logistication [as interpreted], logistication of the detachment. During your evidence yesterday, if my understanding was correct, you mentioned that, in logistical terms, the detachment was receiving symbolic assistance from the army. You described that it had its own logistics, and you mentioned some humanitarian organisations which the detachment had established, itself. Can you tell us briefly how this worked, if you know?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: As for its logistics, the detachment was left to its own devices, in a way. Any support that came from the army was very sporadic and insufficient, if I may put it that way. Everything the detachment required, in terms of food, clothing, weapons and the like, was bought by using donations that we had secured from abroad in most cases. Speaking of the humanitarian organisations that I referred to in my statement, their assistance was used to get certain special items that couldn't be obtained in Bosnia, so they had to be obtained from abroad, such as signals equipment and the like.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 72 of your statement, you say that it was Muatez who decided which sort of military equipment would be purchased and which not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 143, you say that you obtained vehicles, yourself, for the purposes of the detachment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes. Vehicles were purchased both domestically and abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 84, you say that you received some salaries, the amount being 110 [as interpreted] Deutsche mark, but you had no idea where the money had come from; right? You remember that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, it was 80 Deutsche mark, not 110.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I said "100" and the transcript reflects "110," but you say 80. All right. Can the witness now please be shown Exhibit 782. Witness, this is another document entitled: "Information produced by the Security Service Administration of the 3rd Corps." The date is 20th of June, 1995. Please focus on paragraph 2. It talks about contact being established between Ebu Meali and Ebu Ejub. I quote: "In a conversation, Ebu Meali informs Ebu Ejub that a group of Bosniaks is coming and to give them a 15-day rest, 100 Deutsche mark, and three kilograms of meat." So is it true that funds for salaries were secured by the detachment, itself, as this document might lead us to conclude?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: In addition to the salaries that were paid to the detachment, sometimes monetary assistance would be granted to certain members of the detachment, in keeping with what was actually possible and in keeping with the needs of each individual. Likewise, after every operation, the war booty, in terms of weapons, would be estimated in financial terms, and then this would be divvied up and distributed to whoever had been involved in the operation itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All these funds were actually secured by the detachment command, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. I'm moving on to something different now. But before I do, I would like us to see a video clip now. It's the same one that the OTP showed you yesterday. I have it here as P6199, but actually it's Exhibit A33. Could my learned friends from the OTP please play the video, since their version has subtitles? Could you please play back to us General Delic's speech? [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You testified about this clip yesterday, and you said that the atmosphere prevailing in this video clip did not reflect the actual situation when you were there. First of all, do you agree that this took place on the 1st of January, 1996, in a certain institution, and where was that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, it was a huge hall, a sports hall of the army hall in Zenica. It's in a neighbourhood known as "Mokusnica" if that means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does a single shot from this video show this gym hall or sports hall where you say the ceremony actually took place?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, nothing even remotely like what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. I would like to see the videotape at the point when Mr. Delic speaks and behind him we see sort of a cupboard or a shelf, a bookshelf, something that looks like a bookshelf. May I please see that excerpt, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is something that I needed to have clarified. Can you please play again General Delic's speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's right, I'm only interested in the excerpt when General Delic speaks. And also in view of what the witness told us yesterday, that is, that the ceremony took place inside and not outside, therefore the scene does not correspond to what he remembered, so I would just like to clarify that point because the speakers were maybe speaking inside a building and maybe there were some people outside. So I would just like to clarify that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, it might take us a moment to find that actual part of the videotape, and perhaps we can do that and Mrs. Vidovic can continue, and we can come back to that in a few moments, once we've identified what we think Your Honour is referring to, just to save some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, may we proceed like that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the event took place at a farewell ceremony in an enclosed space; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and nobody stood outside. They were all inside. Everybody could come inside the hall or they were staying in the -- standing in the corridor or on the stairs in front of the hall, but nobody was standing outside, and nobody outside could hear what was actually going on in the hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw on the video different scenes of speeches. You can see the speakers, you can see the mass or the crowd, you can see the Mujahedin with their flag. Please, were you ever present -- did you see or hear General Delic address the Mujahedin at any occasion anywhere, other than this event that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: This is the first time that I personally saw General Delic, and I believe that the other members of the detachment had never seen him before, either, never mind have him address them, except on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand the answer. The question was: "Please, were you ever present -- did you see or hear General Delic address the Mujahedin at any occasion anywhere, other than this event that you mentioned?" Now, I underline those last words. Now, the answer says: "This is the first time that I personally saw General Delic ..." I'm not quite sure which first time is this is. Now, in court, or at that location that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to this occasion that I was talking about, January 1st, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for the clarification. From what I understand, the OTP has found -- please, can you now play this segment that Her Honour Judge Lattanzi asked for.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now I would like you to look at this scene. Her Honour, Judge Lattanzi, asked you about that, and I believe that Judge Lattanzi will have more questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, you see General Delic here, and you see an enclosed space, and you see a bookcase or a cupboard there. Does this image correspond to the part of the location where the ceremony took place?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, this doesn't resemble it at all. You can see General-- the general sitting here. He was actually giving a speech. There was a microphone in front of him in the hall itself of the army hall. There was quite a large stage. There were no cupboards or book bookshelves or cases, anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what the witness said was that he gave the speech standing up, and this was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the witness's view of this picture? Does he say this person is standing or is he still sitting? And if, whichever position he takes, can he explain why?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: What I can see here is that he is sitting, and that is the position of the body, and the hands are -- or arms are leaning on a desk.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, Witness, please, you saw the speech with your own eyes. Is this an image -- does this photograph with this cupboard correspond to that image of the stage that you mentioned where this speech was given from?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, this does not resemble the image of that stage, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we run the tape a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that still be in the same speech?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand the question well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it still the same speech, the same occasion where you said he was standing -- or sitting, rather, with his arms on a desk which I didn't see? Is it the same occasion, would you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's not the same occasion. This is happening in the open. You can see trees in the background, and this is not how it was at that farewell ceremony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I don't see trees. I see lines. Are they trees or do you know? So is it your testimony, sir, that what we see here is a different occasion from what we saw a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I'm getting confused now. Are we to understand that neither this picture, nor the former picture where he was sitting, neither of these two pictures were actually taken from the farewell party on 1st January 1996 in Zenica; is that what we are to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour, neither one. And I just wanted to clarify something in relation to your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, no image in this video footage corresponds to the situation in which this other speech was given; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm happy for the witness to answer the question, and then I'd like to put some comments on the record, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, no scene. Yesterday, when we were looking at the earlier part of the tape, the stage where General Sakib Mahmuljin is speaking, you can see President Izetbegovic standing next to him, and he wasn't present either. So this does not correspond, absolutely, to what was actually happening then. No image from the video footage does correspond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm reluctant to intervene at this point, but I do believe it's necessary in order to avoid any unnecessary confusion. When the Prosecution initially filed its motion on 25 September 1997 to add this clip to its exhibit list, our position was quite clear, and it's stated in paragraph 2 of that motion. I'm not going to indicate what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Our position was quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Madam Vidovic, sorry, your opposite number stood up while you were asking --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm concerned that now, with this explanation, of course the Prosecutor will influence the witness. I do not want the witness to hear this explanation. We all know what it says in the submission, but I think that in this way the Prosecutor can interfere or influence the answers by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's precisely why I'm referring to the paragraph numbers of our written pleading, where the Prosecution's position is quite clear on this point. That was all I was going to say, so that we can avoid any unnecessary confusion regarding what this clip is, and I have nothing further to say. And of course I'm not going to say anything that would taint the witness's testimony, but I do refer you back to our initial filing on the 25th of September, 2007, where the Prosecution view was quite clear on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe we could ask the witness if he knows which occasion this live clip is then from, because it appears as if the footage of General Delic seems to correspond to the written words, the movements of his mouth seem to be those that actually came down in the transcript. So it looks, at least from this clip, as if this is a live recording of General Delic's speech and what we see on the transcript corresponds to what he's actually saying in the video, so the issue is now: Does the witness know which occasion this was, if it was not on the 1st of January?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you earlier if the General addressed the El Mujahid. Do you know at all where these images were taken, what occasion it was?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Well, let me say again that General Delic never addressed members of the detachment. As for this footage, I think I know where it comes from. I think this is from the ceremonial lineup --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are requested to repeat your answer, sir. The interpreters didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already said and I repeat, General Rasim Delic never addressed the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment except on the occasion on the 1st of January, 1996, in the hall of the army in Zenica. I believe that this footage is from a ceremonial review of the army in Zenica, which was not attended by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: This footage was shown several times on Bosnia and Herzegovina Television.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to repeat the question. I asked the witness: What was the basis of his testimony regarding to the location of this speech, and the witness then answered that this was shown several times on television. Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It was shown on Bosnia and Herzegovina Television, and even in the corner of the image you can see that there is the TV "BiH" logo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we can focus on the upper right-hand corner. I don't know if that's possible. All right. I would like to put more questions to you about this footage.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to put two or three short questions to you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what I understood, you did not recognise the voice of General Delic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct. I said that the voice was very like his voice, but I cannot assert that that was actually the voice of General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I -- Your Honours, the witness answered that the voice slightly resembles, but here it's entered as "very much resembles." It's opposite from what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please repeat, in relation to the voice, what you said?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, it resembles the voice of General Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, thank you very much. Would this be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, very well, and I will continue with two or three questions in relation to this after the break. Perhaps I can put two short questions now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, what you said yesterday is that Delic held, on that occasion -- or gave on that occasion an appropriate -- a suitable speech, and then you said, "What I heard on the video did not resemble that situation." And based on that, I conclude that you did not recognise the speech of General Delic in that speech that was played on this video.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was a known fact that the Mujahedin did not like NATO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was not an opportunity to mention NATO forces and to address NATO forces during a farewell address to them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct. When I listened to this video, this seemed very inappropriate to me for an occasion such as that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would remember that he said something like that on that occasion on the 1st of January, 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I believe that I would have remembered it, because that would grate on one's ears considerably.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember that, and you also did not hear him talking about command and control in the detachment on that occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and it seems to me not to make sense like that. The detachment was already dismantled and most people left Bosnia and Herzegovina within two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to the Trial Chamber, but I have been asked by Sense, who are broadcasting this hearing, that the public is very interested in listening to this, and this is why I tried to finish a little bit earlier before the actual break, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand that last paragraph. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to ask some questions that have to do with the attitude or the relationship between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in your testimony, the Prosecutor - and also when you were giving the statement and in the preparation for your testimony - showed you many orders from the 3rd Corps that had to do with the El Mujahedin Detachment. In connection with those orders, I would like to ask you the following, you personally: In relation to the orders from the Corps did not -- in connection thus with those orders, did not communicate with members of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes. The documents that were shown were documents that I saw for the first time when the Prosecutor showed them to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you documents that had to do with joint actions of the detachment and members of the 3rd Corps, and in connection with that, I would like to clarify certain matters. It's not in dispute that the El Mujahedin Detachment fought in actions, including actions in July and September 1995, and some other actions that you mentioned. However, you would agree with me that the detachment did not participate in those actions then, when the Corps ordered it, but when this decision was made by the Shura or the Emir; would that be a fair conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The decision about when there would be an action was taken, in principle, by the staff of the detachment, headed by Muatez; in principle, of course. That was the rule. Those who made the preparations for the operations would decide when the detachment would be ready for action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have just said -- well, you mentioned preparations. Am I correct if I believe that the detachment fought pursuant to the plan drafted by that special unit for preparation and planning or the Emir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The detachment, itself, planned absolutely everything that had to do with the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We saw some orders where it says, for example, the detachment should take part in an action according to the plan of the 35th Division. When it participated in actions, did the detachment fight pursuant to the division plan or pursuant to its own plan?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The detachment executed operations according to its own plans. I believe that the purpose of the action or the plan was to inform other units that the detachment was planning or executing such-and-such an action at such-and-such a sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. At this point, I would like you to look at document P1726.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document. I would like to say that this is an order by the 3rd Corps Command of the 3rd of April, 1994, ordering the resubordination of units. I would like you -- and now -- yes, very good. If we can now please look at paragraph 1. According to -- this is the time in which, thus, you were a member of the detachment; is that correct? And this order refers to the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, would you agree that it says in the document, on the basis of need to join the units or unify the units, link up the units more easily, and because of the system of control and command: "I order the El Mujahedin Detachment ..." And then something: "... SDB to be resubordinated to the 330th Light Brigade in all elements of the control and command." And it seems that in the signature, we have Brigadier Mehmed Alagic. Well, what I want to ask you is the following, please: Thus, it is ordered here that the El Mujahedin Detachment, in all elements of control and command, on the day of -- I'm going to ask you to remember this date -- 3rd April, 1994, to be resubordinated to all -- according to all elements of command and control to the 330th Light Brigade. Please, it's correct, isn't it, that this resubordination is de facto -- is something that de facto never happened?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: This is the first time that I am seeing this order. I am aware that members of the detachment took over a section of the line from the 330th Brigade on the Tisa feature, but there was no resubordination of any sort to the Command of the 330th Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there was no resubordination that took place. The detachment never entered under the command of this brigade, as was ordered?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, it can, but can we just see the heading of the document in the English. And may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 845.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be put away, please. At this point, I would like the witness to look at P1727.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, Witness, if we can just look at the beginning of the -- oh, we can see. This is a document of the 3rd Corps of the 5th of April -- the 3rd Corps Command of the 5th of April, 1994. Can we please look at the place where the signature is. Judging by the document, it seems to be signed by the corp commander, but now I would like to go back to the first page of this document because I want to ask you about a fact. You probably have not seen this order before you said that, but I would like to ask you about the fact that has to do with the El Mujahedin Detachment. It's quoted in this order. Your Honours, if we can go back to page 1. You can see that on the 5th of April, 1994, the Command of the Corps is issuing an order for the formation of OG-3 North, whose composition should, among other units, also include the El Mujahedin Detachment. This is page 2 in the English, Your Honours, page 2, 2, page 2 of the English version. And, Witness, what I would like to ask you is the following: We saw earlier just now a document with the date the 3rd of April, 1994, just two days ordering the resubordination to the 330th Brigade. That is what I asked you to remember, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now we have a document of the 5th of April, 1994, here ordering the formation of Operations Group North. That should also include the El Mujahedin Detachment. It says that the OG North Commander should be Mr. Musinbegovic, Jusuf. What I want to ask you is the following: It's correct, isn't it, that the El Mujahedin Detachment never joined the organic composition of OG-3 North; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: This document was already shown to me when I was giving my statement to representatives of the OTP. That was the first time I saw it, and I am not aware that such an order was made under which the El Mujahedin Detachment should become part of OG-3 North. Definitely, the El Mujahedin Detachment was not a part of OG-3 North. We did carry out some operations in the operations zone of the OG-3 North, but we were never a part of OG-3 North.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusuf Musinbegovic never commanded the El Mujahedin Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, he never commanded the El Mujahedin Detachment. I mentioned in my statement that on one occasion at a meeting, Jusuf Musinbegovic ordered the detachment to take part in one operation, and this is something that Muatez smoothly refused to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You wrote that in paragraph 66 of your statement, and you said that "Commander Musinbegovic was in charge of the whole operation. However, our detachment did not take part in that operation because Muatez refused that because the El Mujahedin Detachment was not ready for that." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The detachment not only did not accept the order on the resubordination to OG-3 North, as was ordered, but according to that order, the commander did not even enter into combat actions?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, what is correct is that the detachment, three weeks or a month later, carried out this action independently, without any order?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please show 1831 to the witness. But before that, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 846.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have P1831 on the screen? For the transcript, while waiting for the English translation, I wanted to say that this is an official note of the security organ of the 330th Brigade, dated the 8th of October, 1994. This document deals with some events at Visoka Glava and Pisana Jelika, and you've answered to some of the Prosecutor's questions regarding these two locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please read paragraph 2 of the document, which begins with: "On the 7th of October, 1994 ..." Read it to yourself, please. The document mentions a meeting between members of the 330th Brigade and the El Mujahedin Detachment members at the front line, during which contact was established between an operative from the 330th Brigade and OG North, as well as the El Mujahedin Detachment. That operative, as one could see from the document, tried to persuade Emir that he had certain orders from the commander. In the document, it is stated that the Emir of the El Mujahedin Detachment took that man's rifle away and that the interpreter interpreted that Emir gave a certain order to the member of the 330th Brigade to pick up his radio set and call his commander. What I want to ask you concerning this is the following: It seems that the Emir of the detachment, in the field, orders members of the 330th Brigade around, rather than the other way around?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Such situations occurred frequently. After the operation, some local units had to assume the positions previously taken over by the El Mujahedin Detachment. However, they would usually be late, and I believe that was the reason for this incident as well. This clearly shows that the detachment was not resubordinated to the 330th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, could we please assign an exhibit number to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 847.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 67 of your statement, you said that, and I quote: "Orders came from the 3rd Corps, but as for the El Mujahedin Detachment, Commander Muatez had the final authority to make decisions about whether or not to take part in an operation." I just would like to clarify something. This authority was not given to Muatez by the Command of the 3rd Corps, was it?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct. I think we addressed that already. His authority derived from the Command of the El Mujahedin Detachment, from the Emir and the Shura.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the authority was given to him by the Emir and Shura, and he followed that through; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show P1731 to the witness now. For the transcript, this is a document from the 3rd Corps Command. The date is the 9th of April, 1994. Again, there is a resubordination of the El Mujahedin unit that is being ordered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this is the third order within the period between the 3rd of April, 1994, and the 9th of April, 1994, ordering that the El Mujahedin Detachment be resubordinated? Could you please go to page 2 in the English. Scroll up so that we can see the text. This time, on the 9th of April, 1994, the resubordination of the El Mujahedin Detachment is being ordered to the Command of the 7th Muslim Brigade for the forthcoming combat operations. I wanted to ask you this concerning this document and in general: During the time when you were there, that is, as of the moment you joined the detachment until the end of the war, did the 7th Muslim Brigade Command act as the El Mujahedin Detachment Command at any point?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The detachment was never resubordinated to the Command of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and the Command of the 7th Brigade had held no sway, no authority, over the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw these three documents and a number of others, and I'd like to put my case to you. The documents which came from the 3rd Corps and the orders by which the 3rd Corps attempted to include the El Mujahedin Detachment within the corps structure were basically just pieces of paper. The detachment never accepted such orders or any resubordination?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've told us already that the Command of the detachment decided whether they would participate in a certain operation based on their own criteria applied to the preparation of that action or operation?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the 3rd Corps could not count with the El Mujahedin Detachment when they would need it, when they thought the detachment should participate in a given operation?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 848.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct, is it not, that the detachment accepted to participate in certain operations by putting certain conditions first; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct. Those conditions mainly had to do with the technical preconditions to carry out the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are "technical preconditions"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that the El Mujahedin Detachment always carried out operations within the areas of responsibility of other army units. All those defence lines of the army were mined, and mines and minefields should be cleared first so that members of the detachment could safely enter the area between the two front lines. It also entailed making new paths and roads to be used to pull out casualties and to transport supplies and support.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 208, you described or stated that Muatez insisted, concerning the Al Kamara operation, or Al Kamari -- I'm sorry if I'm pronouncing it wrong. In any case, he asked that all the other units should not act independently but under the Command of the detachment. This was not a technical issue but an issue of the Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes. While answering the previous question, I thought we were still discussing our operations in the Teslic theatre, which was within the OG North area of operation. We haven't reached Vozuca by that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A part of my transcript -- a part of my question was not recorded, and I will repeat it. I reminded you of paragraph 208 of your statement, whereby you said that Muatez, concerning the Al Kamari operation, insisted that the other units involved should not act independently and that they should be under the command of the detachment. Then I said that it was not a technical issue, but rather it had to do with command?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On occasion, the detachment would cancel its participation in certain operations that had been planned?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show Exhibit 396 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you have never seen this document. It is a document from the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 2nd of June, 1995. It has to do with the engagement of the El Mujahedin Detachment within the area of responsibility of the 35th Brigade. And on the 2nd of June, 1995, it is ordered that the El Mujahedin Detachment be resubordinated to the Command of the 35th Division and engage it in accordance with the plan of the Commander of the 35th Division. I would like to ask you this -- Your Honours, could we please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have here a summary of the contents of certain letters that were sent to Saudi Arabia. There is a mention made of Imad as being the person who drafted the letter. Please read to yourself the first paragraph and then let me know when you are done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Imad" is actually Imad Al Misri [phoen] for whom in your statement you said was in charge of the detachment communications; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is sending a report expressing his position by stating that the detachment is formally within the structure of the army, but he says: "They cannot order us into action without our own will." He also states that the detachment puts forth plans for actions, since the army has no experience in that. You will agree with me that this document reflects accurately what you have testified about yesterday and today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you agree with me that the detachment worked like this, in practical terms, at least from the moment that you joined to the end of the war; it worked like this, didn't it: In formal terms, it was under the army command, but in practical terms it made its own plans and the army was in no position to order anything; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this one away. Thank you. I'm moving on to another set of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you made to the OTP, you say that you were involved in combat activities in September 1995. Perhaps you can still recall the second day of this particular action, the 11th of September, 1995. So can you?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown map number 17 from the map book. Before we look at the map, may I just ask you this:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the exact disposition of the El Mujahedin Detachment at about noon? Where were the groups belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment on the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I'm able to recall their positions. I was there, myself, and I know and remember clearly where the groups were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you share that with us, please. Tell us, first of all, and then we'll try to pinpoint the exact positions on the map.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: At noon on the second day of this operation, the 11th of September, the El Mujahedin Detachment was preparing to continue operations in the Kvrge area. Therefore, the detachment was supposed to crush enemy lines in the Kvrge area and continue to advance down the territory and in a northerly direction towards Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the previous location was? What about Djurica Vis, was that the previous location before Kvrge, or on the 11th of September, 1995, had you already reached Kvrge by noon or by around noon? Could we please zoom in slightly --

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- for us to see the Kvrge area?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The upper half of the map. It's fine like this. A little further up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is all right. Can we keep it like this, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please circle "Kvrge" by using the electronic pen?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were at Kvrge at around noon. Can you tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: The detachment units, at noon, carried out an attack against the Serb-held positions around Kvrge. They continued to push forward until that evening. They had taken the area around Vukadino Brdo and Nemici [phoen] village, and Vukadinov Brdo itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you questions about the POWs who were taken in Kesten village on that day. Can you please mark that village for us, if you can see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Perhaps if we pull the map down a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think we can do that, but I think you should be able to see the village. There. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that at noon groups belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment were in this combat area. Was a single group belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment, from noon onwards, still in the Kesten village area, based on your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: What I'm about to say applies to that entire day and later on. Not a single group belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment was in the Kesten village area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 263 of your statement, you say that it's not true that members of the El Mujahedin Detachment took POWs away from any other units, and then you go on to state that you remember that no unit of the 328th Brigade -- or that one unit of the 328th Brigade reported that some members of the El Mujahedin Detachment had arrived and taken charge of POWs. You go on to state that you believe that they had simply fabricated this story in order to receive money in return for these prisoners. And now, finally, I'm coming to the crux of my question. Witness, are you certain that the El Mujahedin Detachment did not seize, take away, capture, whatever you like, those prisoners on that day, those 61 prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I am entirely certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is quite a large number of prisoners we're looking at. You would have been in a position to find out about this. Would you know?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I certainly would have found out. It entirely impossible that anything like this should have happened unbeknownst to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed a great many groups, groups of Arabs, fighting in Central Bosnia throughout 1994 and 1995. You said that those groups had nothing to do with the El Mujahedin Detachment, did you not? Right. And now my question: It is true, isn't it, that the El Mujahedin Detachment was not the only Arab group; that on the 11th of September, 1995, fought in the Vozuca area?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That's true, we were not the only group there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Abu Zubeir's group, about Hamdala, and you said you were aware of the existence of those groups. Do you know that on that day, those groups were involved in this same combat area?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that on the previous day, the 10th of September, they were there, because I personally met some members of Abu Zubeir's group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Personally met. What exactly do you mean by that? You saw them or perhaps you met them in order to arrange something. Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I saw them. We did not arrange anything with them. They were not working with the El Mujahedin Detachment in that particular operation. As I said in my statement, I do not know that they worked with any other military unit, either, but I did realise that they were present in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a large number of humanitarian workers were involved in the fighting with Abu Zubeir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I had heard of this, of the fact that some humanitarian workers were working with Abu Zubeir, but I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the map be given an exhibit number, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 849.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 343 now. Thank you. Exhibit 343. All right. We see that now. I'm not sure how we can follow the translation of this document. Perhaps it will be a more practical idea to put this on the ELMO and show the English on our screens. No. Oh, well. All right. Be that as it may, at this point in time, what I care about is this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a map produced by one of the persons involved in this battle. This person drew a map showing the Mujahedin attack on Ozren and Vozuca in 1995. Based on this diagram -- and you see the key to the diagram. You see that the thick black line shows the movement of Abu Zubeir's groups, whereas the somewhat paler, brighter line, at least according to this person, shows the advance of the El Mujahedin Detachment in the actual battle. Much along the same lines, we see that Abu Zubeir's groups had arrived from Kalesija across Orahovo, Vares, and then Breza in Zenica, and then from Gluha Bukovica and the area of Zeljezno Polje. They linked up as soon as they reached the Vozuca front line. That's what the explanation says. Are these the same locations that you referred to as the places where Abu Zubeir's groups were deployed, Gluha Bukovica and the Zeljezno Polje area?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That's right. I know that Abu Zubeir's headquarters was at Zeljezno Polje. He personally was based there. They had another group at Gluha Bukovica. I said already that I was not aware of the Kalesija group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now is it true, that is at least what the map appears to indicate, isn't it, that Abu Zubeir's groups were moving nearly in parallel with the El Mujahedin unit throughout these combat operations? Can you comment on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: These arrows marking the moves of the El Mujahedin Detachment are not really perfectly accurate. The entire map is a little simplified, but I can say for certain that the detachment was not using these axes, was not moving along these axes displayed here. Well, in part, it was, but not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you know that on the 10th and 11th of September, 1995, Abu Zubeir's group was moving to, along these axes, between Vozuca and Ozren along with some humanitarian workers?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That was where we came across them, at the foot of Paljenik, roughly speaking, and that's what the arrows indicate. Perhaps a little higher up, a little higher up. A little further to the east, perhaps, in a place called "Stog." Those who were involved claimed that they continued from Stog on down this axis. If that's what they claim, then it's probably like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying "Stog," Witness, but we can't follow that. Can you please, at least roughly, mark on this map where it was that you met Abu Zubeir's group?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: [Marks] Somewhere in this area, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also hear that on the 11th of September, Abu Zubeir's group was moving towards Ozren also?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: As far as I know, they remained in the area until the very end of that operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "in the area," can you try to be more specific, sir? Which area do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: I mean the area in which combat operations continued north of Vozuca, between Prokop and as far as Ozren and further beyond.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's try to further clarify this. Abu Zubeir's groups, or indeed humanitarian workers, at the time, were not under the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment, were they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They weren't even working together with the El Mujahedin Detachment during these combat operations, were they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: We didn't even know they were there until we actually bumped into them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, may the map please be given -- or, rather:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, just please write "Stog" or whatever you say was the name of that particular location.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This map has been exhibited already, but we want this map as a new exhibit marked in the way the witness has just marked it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 850.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this away now, please. Could the witness please be shown 669, Exhibit 669. This is entitled: "Information by the Security Service Department." The date is the 16th of September, 1998. Again, this discusses information on the El Mujahedin Detachment. Towards the bottom of this document, if we could please pull the English down a little, what you can see is this: Another intercepted report from the El Mujahedin Detachment, the 16th of September, 1995. I believe I said that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said so, but the interpreter said "1998."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In English, it's the following page. This is about an intercepted report by the detachment's Emir. This is about the Bedr Al Bosna, it's the battle of Vozuca, the liberation of Vozuca. And now I want the witness to look at page 2 of the Bosnian and page 4 of the English. We can show the Bosnian in such a way as to see the bottom half of the page. Oh, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, focus your attention on the part that says: "New territory has been taken ..." That is the second-to-last paragraph. In the English, it starts with the following words: "We have taken new territories ..." It's just that one portion. Do you agree that it reads: "The Mujahedin have gained ground and entered a group of Serbian villages. After the killing, they took 60 prisoners." Please keep this in mind as we proceed. Do you agree that it says here "the Mujahedin," which is not necessarily the same thing as "the Mujahedin Detachment"; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will need to go back to this. It has not been interpreted properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I asked the witness is this, and I will try to say this slowly. I asked the witness this: Do you agree that what the document says is this: The Mujahidi [as interpreted] have gained ground and entered a group of Serbian villages or Serb villages, and do you agree here that -- that what we discussed yesterday, Mujahidi and Mujahedin "odred" is not the same thing, is it?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Of course it's not the same thing. We concluded that yesterday, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Mujahidi" is a general term for a fighter; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Realtime transcript read in error
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the English version, it reads "the Mujahedin," which is certainly not what the Bosnian says. I was waiting until we had a witness here who could clarify that for our benefit.
